newsitem.title: UK: Dixons down on warranty tax worries.
newsitem.headline: Dixons down on warranty tax worries.

text.p: Shares in British electrical gods retailer Dixons were indicated lower in pre-market trade on Wednesday on worries that tax increases on warranties announced in Tuesday's budget could hit profits.
Dixons shares, which weakened on Tuesday in the aftermath of the budget, were marked 10p lower at 540-1/2p.
Others in the sector were marked lower. Kingfisher, owner of retailer Comet, was at 620p after a 624-1/2p close.
The Financial Times influential Lex column warned that the move to impose value-added-tax on extended warranties could "knock five to 10 percent off Dixons' profits".
Among other firms mentioned by Lex as likely casualties of the proposed tax on warranties, television rental firm Thorn was down 10p at 274p.
